title: Ground penetrating radar finds unmarked graves at Newside Cemetery - NewsBreak
text: LOWER PAXTON TWP., Pa. (WHTM) — Documents show 48 early settlers are buried at Newside Cemetery, but there are only 19 tombstones within a fenced-in area. The graves date back to the 1740s to 1856. Newside Cemetery Restoration Project co-chair Jay Purdy says veterans are buried here who fought in the French and Indian War, War of 1812, and Revolutionary War. When Utility Services Group heard veterans were laid to rest in the cemetery, the company donated its ground penetrating radar services to help locate the grave sites. “What it does, it goes down, finds something underneath the subsurface and bounces back up and it will give you a signal,” says project manager Jerry Contino. “By the length of time it takes for that pulse to come back on, the receiver will tell you about the depth.” Twenty-three have been found so far. Volunteers had to come in first and help clear brush from the cemetery and its surrounding area. “We’ve found them,” says project co-chair Jay Purdy. “These people have not been recognized for 200 years. They’re going to be recognized now.” The Lower Paxton Township Historical Commission says the original tombstones were moved in the late 1800’s to allow farming. “We feel that these markers were placed here probably back in the 1920s when the Daughters of the American Revolution put the large scale monument with all the names,” says project co-chair David Doyle. “We know that some of the people that were buried here originally were Paxton Boys and then they became heroes during the Revolutionary War.” The project restoration co-chairs hope to have a plaque installed that teaches people about the history of those who are laid to rest in Newside Cemetery. A rededication ceremony will be held in 2026. Download the abc27 News+ app on your Roku, Amazon Fire TV Stick, and Apple TV devices The project’s next goal is removing trees that could fall on the existing cemetery. The location of the Newside Church is still a mystery. The commission says radar found evidence of two buildings, but there’s no indications either was a church.
